comment: Known appliances and the LCDproc driver that lights their built-in panel.
Same shape and the same discipline as os-linkhealth's chassis.json: match on SMBIOS, propose
a driver and its options, and say plainly how far the proposal has actually been proven. An
entry is a claim about a machine we cannot see, so every one of them carries a 'confirmed'
line written by whoever watched the screen light up - or left empty, which means nobody has.
Nothing here is applied on its own. The settings page offers the match as a starting point and
the owner presses Apply. A wrong driver writing to the wrong serial port is not a mistake a
plugin should make on its own initiative, and a serial port on an unknown appliance may be
somebody's console.
Matching uses kenv smbios values, exactly as os-linkhealth does. maker/product/version are
regular expressions. The first entry whose every stated field matches wins; 'generic' is the
fallback and proposes nothing at all.
The 'drivers' table below is only a fallback. config.py prefers /usr/local/etc/LCDd.conf.sample,
which the lcdproc package installs and which lists, section by section, every option each
driver really understands. Reading the installed package beats trusting a table copied into
this file, which would rot the first time LCDproc gained an option.

sophos-xg-3xx.confirmed: XG 330 rev 2 (smbios version 330r2), 2026-09-21: the display is verified - LCDd initialised the panel with no errors and the owner photographed live CPU, memory and uptime screens on it. The keypad is verified too: all four keys reported, measured one button at a time at ReportLevel 5 with the screen held still, three presses and three events each. The map above is that measurement and not LCDproc's default order, which puts Enter on 4,1 - where this panel has its down arrow.
notes: ConnectionType=ezio fixes the line at 2400 baud by itself - the driver reported 'serial: using speed: 2400' with no Speed option set, so this entry deliberately does not write one.
Heartbeat must stay off. This panel has no programmable character for LCDproc's heartbeat glyph and draws it as a solid black block in the corner.
DelayMult=2 is what the owner settled on after trying 4: faster, and with RefreshDisplay redrawing the whole screen every few seconds it has not dropped a character.
The panel is printed with a down arrow, ESC, an up arrow and ENTER, in that order, and that is the order of the matrix positions above.

At 2400 baud the display and the keypad share the line: with screens changing every 3 seconds and a full redraw every 4, two thirds of the presses were lost. A quiet screen is what makes this keypad reliable: hold the screen still while measuring the keys, and keep the redraw interval wide on a panel whose keys are used.

sophos-xg-family.display: Sophos XG / XGS (panel not confirmed on this model)
comment: A Sophos box whose exact model we have not watched. The hardware is close enough that the
same proposal is worth offering, but it is offered as a guess and labelled as one: the
settings page shows the empty 'confirmed' line and says nobody has seen this work yet.
sophos-xg-family.hint: Nobody has confirmed this model yet. Press Test after applying: if the panel stays dark, try the driver list - mtc_s16209x lights a screen of this shape and cannot read a button, which is the honest fallback. The key map is copied from the XG 330 rev 2 and is a guess here: measure it with the key test before you trust which button is which.

generic.hint: No proposal for this machine. Choose a driver and a serial port by hand - the page lists the drivers this installation of LCDproc actually carries and the ports this machine actually has - then press Test. Sending a report of what worked is how this table grows.

comment: Fallback only, used when /usr/local/etc/LCDd.conf.sample is missing. Every option name here
was read out of that sample on the reference machine (lcdproc 0.5.9_1), not remembered.
A driver absent from this table is not refused: config.py writes what the panel entry asks
for and says in its answer that it could not check the option names.
Where each adjustable speed from the settings page lands in LCDd.conf. The three server
options exist whatever the driver is. The two driver options do not: DelayMult belongs to
hd44780 and sed1520 only, RefreshDisplay to hd44780 only, and writing either into a section
that has never heard of it makes LCDd complain on every start. config.py checks the driver's
real option list before writing them, and reports the knobs it had to leave out.
